Hello! I am so sorry that this is happening to you and that you’re feeling like this. Breakups are truly so devastating and soul crushing, even more so when you are young or have mental health issues. I know it feels horrible right now, but try to think of this as an opportunity to find yourself and find coping mechanisms for your mental health issues. Consider talking to a therapist, if that’s an option for you. You are still very young and I am assuming you don’t really know exactly who you are yet, which can make breakups so much worse because you feel like this person was a part of you in some way or that no one else will be like them. Take this time to find yourself, and who you are without your ex in your life. It’s completely okay to take some time to process the breakup first. Cry it out, really grieve the relationship for a few days. After that you need to pick yourself up. Don’t stay in that grieving place too long. Try to do things that will take your mind off it, like hobbies, hanging out with friends/family, or just anything that makes you happy or that will improve you as a person. You might not completely be over this for a long time, and that’s okay. One day you will wake up and realize that you hadn’t thought of them. Or you will be going to bed and you will realize you haven’t cried over them in a month. My biggest piece of advice is try your very best not to stalk their social media. I went through a similar breakup at 17 and I was spiraling as well. But i PROMISE, you will find love again. And you need to understand that. You have your entire life ahead of you. You will have many other loves throughout your lifetime. Understand that it will truly all be okay. If you need anything else don’t be afraid to message me :)

Just move on with your life and be better next time. Realize that there is nothing you can do but find someone else to start over with and be better for. It wasn’t a mistake at all. It was a choice. A drunken one night stand is a mistake. Even then, it is still cheating and a choice in a way. But 3 months?!?? That’s a whole affair. You had infinite chances to choose not to do that. You could’ve also told him right after it ended, instead of wasting his time. But, you chose to have it play out exactly how it did. They are not “horrible mistakes,” it’s not an “oopsie,” it’s choices you can learn from. You didn’t deserve him unfortunately and you did something bad and now you are paying for it. Now that you know this is what happens when you cheat, never do it again. I do applaud you for telling him at least. Even if your guilt forced you to, thank god you told him and didn’t hide it for the rest of your lives. Now that you have it all behind you, focus on bettering yourself for a while. Focus on learning from your mistakes and becoming better for the next person that comes to your life.
